title: Trigger links: a person-to-person flow (shared-connect), carried invitation, size budget, registry entry
context: Defines the QR and link form two apps need to share for a contact ceremony between apps.

title: A shared wire core across Trust Task implementations: one test, eight dimensions, and a self-report
context: What every Trust Task implementation must get identical for documents to be readable across apps.

title: Rulings requested: blocked, verdict versus refusal, already-in-state, defaulted quorum, proof bytes, freshness, indeterminate
context: Open rulings in the Trust Tasks specification that decide how two implementations read the same answer.

title: Data rooms: a few requests from the Keyring wallet integration
context: What a second client needs from a Data Room host; relevant for any app joining a room it does not host.

title: A roadmap to Trust Task conformance: layers, profiles and optional modules
context: How a shared conformance suite for Trust Task documents could be layered; the natural home for running procedures between projects (see issue 1 here).

title: Proposal: a libp2p transport binding for Trust Tasks
context: Decides whether projects on libp2p without a mediator share a transport with projects on TSP mediators.

title: VMC: allow a VTN's members to be VTCs or VTNs, and keep nested membership per-hop
context: Sets how a membership credential names a community that is itself a member of a trust network; affects what another app checks.

title: Two parties at two different mediators: how do they reach each other?
context: Two apps at different TSP mediators cannot reach each other today; decides whether people on different apps can write without agreeing on a mediator.

title: A Trust Task type for a message from one person to another
context: No registry type exists for a message between two people; a shared type with no transferable proof would let two apps exchange messages.

title: A wake endpoint at the mediator: one URL, called when a message is stored for a client that is not connected
context: How a mediator wakes a client that is not connected, without a push provider in the mediator; decides whether a message reaches a person whose app is closed.
